bill.title: WWII Nurses Congressional Gold Medal Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committee on House Administration, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bill.officialSummary: WWII Nurses Congressional Gold Medal Act This bill provides for the award of a Congressional Gold Medal to World War II Army and Navy Nurse Corps members in recognition of their critical military service and devotion to duty.

classification.plainSummary: This bill directs Congress to award a Congressional Gold Medal to the women who served in the Army and Navy Nurse Corps during World War II. The medal would recognize their military service and dedication. This is an honorary measure; it does not create new programs or change existing law beyond authorizing the medal itself.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would provide for the award of a Congressional Gold Medal to World War II Army and Navy Nurse Corps members in recognition of their critical military service and devotion to duty.
plain.whoItTouches: People in the military, and their families.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in service, and what the military buys. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
